newsitem.title: USA: Banc One beefs up munis in East, Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Banc One beefs up munis in East, Midwest.

text.p: Banc One Capital's year-old New York City office coupled with the July 21 acquisition of Chicago-based Fitzgerald Davis & Associates has given the Banc One Corp unit a "tremendous" tax-exempt presence in the Midwest and East Coast, Banc One Capital's vice chairman said.

"A little over a year ago we realized there was tremendous talent in the tax-exempt market in New York," James Chapman, vice chairman and managing director at Columbus, Ohio-based Banc One Capital, said in an interview.

About three weeks ago, Banc One added two more names to its New York City roster, hiring former Dillon Read & Co salesman Howie Burstein and former PNC Bank trader Jerry Cangialosi. Burstein joined Bank One as a vice president of insitutional sales, while Cangialosi came on board as vice president and head trader.

The New York office opened about a year ago when Banc One decided to build a franchise to service institutional accounts and issuers, sources at the firm said. To accomplish that, Banc One launched it's New York office with Bob Isabella, Rich Riccardi, Bob Bergamini and Nick Squitieri, Chapman said. Isabella, Riccardi and Bergamini are senior vice presidents. Squitieri is a vice president.
Rounding out the 10-member New York office are Carl Scotti, Mary Ann Ponti, Joseph Hutchinson and John Vida, all vice presidents of insitutional sales.

"Banc One Capital has always had a very strong presence in the tax-exempt market, and what we are trying to do is increase that presence," Chapman said. "And we further added to that strength by acquiring Fitzgerald Davis in Chicago, which was completed on July 21."
Additional staff may be added, Chapman said.
"We're always looking for opportunities to strengthen our firm," he said. "If the opportunities present themselves, we will be open to additions both in sales and trading."
